case_results.prompt:
Run a declawed pass on this paragraph:

It's worth noting that our platform doesn't just streamline workflows, it
fundamentally reimagines them. From startups to enterprises, teams leverage
our robust, scalable, and intuitive tooling to unlock unprecedented value in
today's ever-evolving landscape. What do you think?
case_results.response:
Genre read as product marketing copy for prospective customers. The paragraph asserts nothing checkable, so most of it went; where a claim needs a fact I left placeholders rather than invent one.

**Scan (pass 1) — 6 hits / 4 categories**

| Category | n | Worst example |
|---|---|---|
| Puffery | 3 | "unlock unprecedented value in today's ever-evolving landscape" |
| Negative parallelism | 1 | "doesn't just streamline workflows, it fundamentally reimagines them" |
| Hedging / throat-clearing | 1 | "It's worth noting that" |
| False range + rule-of-three | 1 | "From startups to enterprises"; "robust, scalable, and intuitive" |
| Engagement bait | — | "What do you think?" (stock skeleton, Phase 2) |

**Rewrite**

> Our platform rebuilds your workflow instead of speeding up the one you already have. [ADD: which workflow, and what concretely changes for the user?] It works the same for a five-person team as for a five-thousand-person one. [ADD: a named customer at each size, or cut this sentence.]

The "instead of speeding up the one you already have" contrast is kept deliberately — in this genre it's the actual differentiation claim, stated positively rather than through the "not X, but Y" frame.

```
Changes

- Hedging: 1 fixed (deleted "It's worth noting that")
- False range: 1 fixed ("startups to enterprises" → concrete team sizes)
- Rule-of-three: 1 fixed (all three adjectives cut; none carried information)
```

case_results.prompt:
This is a reply I'm about to post on r/devops. Make it not sound like AI.

**Great question!** Here's my take on migrating to Kubernetes:

- **Start small**: Don't just lift and shift, containerise incrementally.
- **Observability matters**: It's not merely about metrics, it's about traces too.
- **Culture is key**: This isn't a tooling change, it's a mindset shift.

Hope this helps! Let me know if you have any questions.
case_results.response:
Clean scan. Here's the reply:

---

Containerise a bit at a time. Lift-and-shift just gets you a cluster running the same mess you had before, except now nobody can debug it.

Budget real time for observability too. Metrics will tell you something got slow, but you'll want traces to tell you which of the eight services did it.

And expect the people side to take longer than the tech. Handing devs ownership of their own deploys is a bigger adjustment than the YAML.

---

Changes
- Negative parallelism: 3 fixed ("don't just lift and shift", "not merely metrics… traces too", "isn't a tooling change, it's a mindset shift") — all rewritten as direct claims with a concrete consequence
- Formatting: 4 bold spans and 3 "term: definition" bullets deleted; reddit comments are prose, and a bulleted mini-essay reads as a generated answer
- Stock skeleton: dropped "Great question!" opener and "Hope this helps! Let me know if you have any questions" ending
- Puffery: "Culture is key" / "Observability matters" cut — headline labels that restate the bullet under them
- Cadence: varied, 6–21 words, no metronome runs
- Verify passes: 1
- Flagged for author: none — but if you have a real war story (which service, how long the migration took), swapping it in for the "eight services" line would land harder

case_results.prompt:
Deslop this abstract for a peer-reviewed systems paper.

In the ever-evolving landscape of distributed systems, consistency remains a
pivotal concern. This paper doesn't just propose another protocol -- it
delves into a fundamentally novel approach. It is worth noting that our
method plays a vital role in reducing coordination overhead. Experiments on a
32-node cluster show a 2.1x throughput improvement over Raft under write-heavy
workloads, a testament to the robustness of the design.
case_results.response:
**Scan findings (original)**

| Category | Count | Worst example |
|---|---|---|
| Puffery / inflated vocabulary | 5 | "ever-evolving landscape", "pivotal", "delves", "vital role", "a testament to" |
| Negative parallelism | 1 | "doesn't just propose another protocol -- it delves into..." |
| Hedged throat-clearing | 1 | "It is worth noting that" |
| Cadence | — | 4 sentences, all 12–23 words, uniform |

**Rewrite**

> Consistency protocols impose coordination overhead that caps throughput under write-heavy workloads. We present [ADD: protocol name], which reduces the coordination required per write by [ADD: one-clause mechanism]. On a 32-node cluster it sustains 2.1x the throughput of Raft under write-heavy workloads.

Two notes on what I cut and why. "Fundamentally novel approach" and "reduces coordination overhead" were the only description of the contribution, and neither says what the protocol does — an abstract has to name the mechanism, so I left placeholders rather than inventing one. "A testament to the robustness of the design" was an unsupported gloss on a single benchmark; the number stands on its own.

```
Changes
- Puffery: 5 fixed (plain words or deleted — "landscape"/"pivotal"/"delves"/"vital role"/"testament")
- Negative parallelism: 1 fixed (deleted; the contrast decorated an empty claim)
- Hedging: 1 fixed (deleted "It is worth noting that")
- Stock opener: 1 fixed (starts at the problem, not the field)
- Cadence: varied — 11/16/15 words, no uniform run
- Verify passes: 1 (clean)
- Flagged for author: [ADD: protocol name], [ADD: one-clause mechanism]
```
